case_title.quote: ARVIND KUMAR v. STATE OF NCT, DELHI

number_of_accused.quote: the appellant-accused has taken an exception

accused_gender.quote: I asked Santri Ct.Arvind i.e accused
accused_gender.reason: Male is plausible, but the judgment never states gender explicitly; it is only implied by name and role.

accused_occupation.quote: The appellant was posted as a guard at the Police Station.
accused_occupation.reason: Police guard at the station is stated.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on wealth or class.

victim_gender.reason: The victim is male, as shown by name and 'him'.

victim_religion.reason: Not stated; the name must not be used to infer religion.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: Mohd. Rashid (the deceased) was on duty as “Munshi-Roznamacha”
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Both were police personnel at the same station; the alleged enmity was not established.

offence_category.quote: the appellant is guilty of a lesser offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC
offence_category.reason: The final established offence is negligence; the Court rejected murder and culpable homicide. Murder was only the charged offence.

statutory_provisions.quote: conviction of the appellant under Section 302 of the IPC is set aside and he is held guilty of ... Section 304A
statutory_provisions.reason: Matches the s.302 charge and the s.304A conviction.

evidence_type.quote: There are two witnesses who claim that they were eyewitnesses
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, ballistic, circumstantial and res gestae evidence all appear.

confession.quote: the statement of an accused to which Section 6 is applicable cannot be treated as a confession of guilt
confession.reason: No confession; the statement is not one.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Gross negligence in not keeping the change lever in the safety position while holding an automatic weapon
aggravating_circumstances.quote: there is gross negligence on the part of the appellant which led to a loss of human life
aggravating_circumstances.reason: The Court noted gross negligence, so 'None noted' is not accurate.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: it is not possible to attribute knowledge to him

trial_court_outcome.quote: The Trial Court sentenced the appellant to undergo a life sentence.

high_court_outcome.quote: the conviction of the appellant has been confirmed

final_outcome.quote: he is held guilty of committing the offence punishable under Section 304A
final_outcome.reason: Conviction modified to a lesser offence.

offence_finally_established.quote: guilty of a lesser offence punishable under Section 304A

imprisonment_type.quote: maximum sentence is imprisonment for two years. The appellant has undergone a sentence of more than eight years.
imprisonment_type.reason: The Court treated the sentence as the 2-year maximum, already undergone, so fixed term is reasonable.

imprisonment_years.correct_value: 2 (maximum sentence for s.304A, deemed undergone; no specific sentence stated)
imprisonment_years.quote: The appellant has undergone the maximum sentence prescribed for the said offence.
imprisonment_years.reason: The Court did not expressly impose 2 years; it held the maximum had been undergone.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove the 'Several other persons present did not support the prosecution' evidence-assessment content, which is framed as the Court's finding, and keep the account neutral
neutral_facts.quote: Both PW-6 and PW-17 did not support the prosecution.
neutral_facts.reason: It is mostly accurate but states the initial FIR was on the duty officer's statement without naming the offence. It also refers to 'Eyewitness accounts described... accidental firing', which tilts the account towards the defence.

offence_severity.quote: for which the maximum sentence is imprisonment for two years

attempt_completion.quote: the police personnel ... rushed the deceased to a hospital where he was declared dead
attempt_completion.reason: The offence was completed; death resulted.

physical_harm.correct_value: Death from five bullets fired into the neck (the judgment says neck, and PW-12 says neck and chest)
physical_harm.quote: The deceased got five rounds of bullets in his neck.
physical_harm.reason: The court summary says neck; the neck-and-chest detail comes only from witness testimony.

number_of_offences.quote: Section 302 of IPC was applied while filing the chargesheet
number_of_offences.reason: One charge, s.302; one conviction under s.304A stands.

premeditation_planning.quote: The prosecution has failed to prove that the appellant had either any intention of causing the death

motive.quote: we will have to proceed on the footing that the motive was not proved
motive.reason: Alleged motive marked as not established.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the version of PW-12 and PW-25 ... completely supports the defence of the appellant of accidental firing

witness_credibility.quote: the version of the prosecution about the appellant and PW-12 making such statements does not inspire confidence

post_offence_conduct.quote: the conduct of the appellant of making the said statement becomes relevant in view of Section 6

custody_duration.quote: the appellant had undergone incarceration for a period of about 8 years and 11 months

bail_history.quote: released on bail by this Court by the order dated 27th November 2017

legal_representation.quote: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv., Ms. Prerna Mehta, Adv. for the Appellant.

investigation_status.quote: Section 302 of IPC was applied while filing the chargesheet

procedural_irregularity.quote: the case of the prosecution that he intentionally opened fire by aiming at the deceased was not put to the appellant

prosecution_argument.quote: the appellant certainly had knowledge that the use of SAF carbine may cause death

defence_argument.quote: no offence was committed by the appellant in view of Section 80 of IPC

legal_principle_applied.quote: by no stretch of the imagination, it is a case of culpable homicide as defined under Section 299

sentencing_rationale.quote: his detention in prison is no longer required

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: No intention or knowledge of likely death; accidental firing; maximum sentence already undergone
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: The appellant has undergone a sentence of more than eight years.
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Broadly right, but the long custody is the basis for ending detention, not a mitigating factor as such.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: gross negligence on the part of the appellant
